title: Computing a width-parametric split
statement: Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and let $E$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with time bound $T_E:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Suppose $T_E$ is monotone and, on every Boolean word $s$, $E$ halts within $T_E(|s|)$ steps with output the binary representation of $f(|s|)$. Then there are a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $c$ such that, on every Boolean word $w$, $M$ halts within $c(|w|+1)(T_E(|w|+1)+|w|+2)$ steps and outputs the pair encoding of the prefix and suffix of $w$ cut at the least $i\le |w|$ satisfying $i+f(i)=|w|$; if no such $i$ exists, it outputs the empty word.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
E is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
TE is a natural-number-valued time bound
E computes the binary representation of f(input length) within TE(input length) on every input
replaced:
Let a machine $E$ compute the binary representation of $f$ applied to the
input length within a monotone time bound $T_E$. Then there exist a machine
$M$ and a constant $c$ computing, within
$c\,(n+1)(T_E(n+1) + n + 2)$ steps, the function sending $w$ to the pair
encoding of the split of $w$ at the least $i$ with $i + f(i) = \abs{w}$,
and to the empty word when no such $i$ exists.
